answer.evidence: Column scan at x=8, 16 and 23 shows a light band in rows 1-6 (lavender gradient, then white at row 5 and a pink edge line at row 6). Rows 7-8 below it are a dark eave shadow (L=51). The open shelf face then runs from row 9 to row 29, which is about 21 rows. The band is a canopy/header plane with an edge line and shadow, so it counts as a top surface and not a plain front-facing strip. The shelf boards at rows 13, 19 and 25 are 1-row lips with goods behind them. The side uprights are drawn flat on the south face, so no receding side face is visible.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 21 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 17 for the cheese stall, 20 for the roofed well and 9 for the hedge. Near-flat coverage is 0%, and the stall reference is at 13%, so no large flat fills. 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted (a dark bluish-grey tone against the pale frame) rather than a black sticker line. The shelves are packed with small multi-colour items, and the cabinet frame and striped header show some highlight/mid/shadow stepping. It is slightly flatter and more front-on than the stall and well, and the frame ramp is about 4 steps, which is a little under Beodeul's 5-6. A careful artist would still accept it next to the references.

surfaces.part: header/cornice band with pink sign strip

answer.evidence: The top rows 1-6 are a flat header band: a light gradient with a pink strip at row 6, read as a face-on sign or cornice. It has no ellipse and no receding surface. Rows 7-8 are dark, but they read as the shelf opening rather than eave shadow under a top plane. Below that, the shelves (edge lines at rows 13, 19 and 25) and the products (milk, boxes, cans) are all drawn face-on. The shelf bays show no contents seen from above and no receding top surfaces. The object is a flat front elevation, so any top surface is at most a 1-2 row rim.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small shelf gondola, about one tile wide, with a grey-white frame and rows of pink, blue and white goods. It has 21 visible tones per tile, which is level with the stall (17) and well (20) and above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0% and none of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted. It reads as a dark, bluish-grey tone on the frame and not as a black sticker line. The product rows give some texture, but the frame and the shelf backs are fairly smooth, with fewer graded steps than the references' 5-6 per material. The frame body shows about 3-4 lightness steps. Structurally it is clean and acceptable beside the references, but a little less shaded and grained than the stall and the well.

answer.evidence: Rows 1-5 form a light band, lightest at rows 5-6, which could be read as a top surface. Row 6 is a pink edge line, and rows 7-8 are dark (L=51) like an eave shadow. Below that the open front face runs from row 7 to row 29. It holds the shelves at rows 13, 19 and 25 with goods on them, and a base at rows 26-29. The width profile is a constant 32 and the side strips are just the frame, so no receding side face is drawn. The top reading is borderline, because the band could also be a face-on header board. The edge line plus the shadow rows tip it toward a top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts favour the candidate. It has 21 visible tones per tile, against 17 for the cheese stall, 20 for the roofed well and 9 for the hedge. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted. By eye it reads as a dark slate or blue-grey line, not a black sticker outline. The grey-white frame shows about 4-5 value steps, with a lit top, a header band and a darker side. Each shelf row has small product dots in pink, blue and white, with shelf lips in between. That gives clustered detail comparable to the stall's goods. It is smaller and cleaner than the stall, and its texture is more 'some' than 'rich', but it is not thinner or flatter than the references. A careful artist would accept it next to them.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small shelf unit with a pale frame, a dark top sign band and rows of coloured products. It reads as a gondola and is the same kind as the references (stall, well, bench). Measured facts back it up: 21 visible tones per tile against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted (dark blue-grey/purple-brown) rather than black. The frame has about 4 lightness steps (highlight, light, mid, dark), slightly fewer than Beodeul's 5-6. The product rows add varied dots and clusters, so the surface is not flat, but the shelf backing is somewhat uniform. It would sit acceptably beside the references without looking like a flat sticker.
